hn-50141657.t: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
hn-50141657.s: Online roadblocks are undermining the narrative behind AI agents.
ex: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen. OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen. Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won’t play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users.

hn-50138531.t: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests
hn-50138531.s: The Search API and the Fetch API give agents and RAG applications access to live web content:
ex: The Search API and the Fetch API give agents and RAG applications access to live web content: Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API. See the Search API Reference and Fetch API Reference for the complete request and response schemas. Send your API key and the JSON content type in the request headers: The query is forwarded with its search syntax intact. The examples below combine operators with a search term; you can combine multiple operators in one query. A successful request returns HTTP 200 with a results array. A normal search with no matches returns an empty array. Fetching is subject to the target site's availability and access policies. Errors follow the OpenAI-compatible error format. The param field is always null. Search and Fetch are read-only. For HTTP 408, 429, or 5xx errors, wait and retry. For HTTP 402, top up your account before retrying. Do not retry other 4xx errors without changing the request.

hn-50142573.s: I think good products carry something of the people who make them. Their experience, what they care about, and how they think things should work.
ex: I think good products carry something of the people who make them. Their experience, what they care about, and how they think things should work. You might not know who those people are, but you can feel their perspective in the product. The industry often talks about software as though it comes out of a factory. You collect requirements, build features, and measure whether they work. Follow the process and you should get a good result. Now we're talking automating this whole pipeline with agents. But two teams can talk to similar customers, have access to the same technology, and make very different things. The difference comes from how they understand what they see and the style they go about building it. The founder background or company DNA also shapes this a lot. At Linear, we have always valued intuition over process or data. I think people sometimes understand that as making decisions based on personal preference, without much thought or evidence.

hn-50137950.t: Sphinx – A hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before shipping
hn-50137950.s: A Git hook for agent-assisted development. Before your agent’s code ships, Sphinx asks you a question about what it actually does.
ex: “You can outsource your thinking, but not your understanding.” Sphinx is a Git hook for agent-assisted development. Before your agent’s code ships, it asks you a question about what that code actually does. Built to run on minimal tokens, from your existing coding agent, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Your webhook handler now saves the event ID before calling charge(). Stripe times out and sends the same event again. What happens on the retry? Not quite. The retry finds the saved ID and returns 200 without charging. But that ID is stored before the charge succeeds. If charge() fails, what does the next retry do? An illustrative exchange. Real questions come from your diff. Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi, or plain Git. Your answers never reach the coding agent, and .env files and keys are never opened. In a hurry? sphinx yolo lets pushes through, and every skip is logged.

hn-50141076.s: μRepRap - A 3D printer project designed to work at the micron scale
ex: The RepRapMicron Project, or μRepRap, is an extension of the Open Source RepRap 3D printer project that aims to bring micron-scale fabrication into very widespread adoption. The main project page is here and currently the assembly instructions are on the Github wiki. It uses hardware and software familiar to 3D printer and CNC developers (GCODE, GRBL, NEMA17 steppers etc.), and materials that are easily and inexpensively available. As of PIKA V0.02 pixels can be placed or engraved with repeatable micron precision in 2D without difficulty. Range of motion is approximately 8mm on X, Y, and Z axes. A resin deposition system for <4μm droplets is functional if not complete. Current resin material is "Top Coat" Nail Art UV Gel. Printing with an optical fibre in standard 3D printer resin using a UV LED is also supported. The meaty part is in the "pika" directory, where the OpenSCAD models for a 3D printed print-in-place flexure chassis and axis drivers can be found.

hn-50140001.t: Open MicroManipulator – A sub-micrometer 3D motion control plattform
ex: This project contains an open source low-cost, easy-to-build motorized XYZ Micro-Manipulator motion control platform achieving submicron precision. It's designed for applications such as optical alignment, probing electronic components, and microscopy. Check out the YouTube video for more information about the device and how it is built: An Open Source Motorized XYZ Micro-Manipulator - Affordable sub µm Motion Control Thanks to its parallel kinematic structure and miniature ball joints, it achieves good mechanical stiffness and a large range of motion. The motors are off the shelf stepper motors driven by a 30 kHz closed loop controller and a very precise PWM signal. A 'magnetic gearing' approach increases the resolution of the low-cost magnetic rotary encoders by a factor of 30 allowing for steps down to 50nm (Please mind the difference between resolution and accuracy. The absolute accuracy is significantly worse.

hn-50132278.t: Amazon uses AI to monitor union risk in UK warehouses
hn-50132278.s: Internal documents suggest tech giant collects ‘hundreds of data points’ for ‘union-busting’ AI model
ex: Internal documents suggest tech giant collects ‘hundreds of data points’ for ‘union-busting’ AI model Garfield Hylton has long known that Amazon monitors and logs every minute of his working day. Every product he scans, every second he takes between scans, every time his scanner is briefly inactive – all of it is tracked, recorded, and used to set productivity targets and predictions. But what 62-year-old Hylton didn’t know is that Amazon seemingly also monitors potential “dissent” in the Coventry warehouse where he works, using AI to surveil posts on social media and the company’s internal staff bulletin board. Internal documents made public as part of a court battle between Amazon and a Canadian union suggest the tech giant uses Atlas, an in-house AI forecasting tool, to predict how likely its warehouse staff in the US, Canada and the UK are to attempt to form a union, stage a sit-in, or conduct other “disruptive labour events”.

hn-50141295.t: Tesla 'Cannot Guarantee' Roadster Reservation Holders Will Ever Get a Car
hn-50141295.s: The document customers must sign to reserve a Roadster says Tesla cannot guarantee when—or if—the car will be delivered.
ex: Tesla unveiled its second-generation Roadster for a second time Thursday night, nearly 10 years after the last big shindig. It made even bigger promises to help customers forget that it never delivered that car, despite taking deposits worth up to $250,000 (the full price of the top Founders Series version at the time). Now it appears Tesla is preparing to do the same thing again. InsideEVs noticed that the reservation agreement for the new new Roadster on Tesla’s website states that “Roadster is still under development and so we cannot guarantee when your vehicle will actually be delivered or if it will be delivered.” And while Tesla is, again, asking for up to $250,000 up front, the reservation agreement also states that it is just that. Customers are only getting an “approximate” place in line if the Roadster enters production, not a confirmed build slot.

hn-50144005.t: Florida's HOAs and condo associations are making the housing crisis worse
hn-50144005.s: A housing crisis has three parts: what a home costs, how many are for sale, and whether the people in them get to stay. In Florida the homeowner and condominium associations push on all three.
ex: A housing crisis has three parts: what a home costs, how many are for sale, and whether the people in them get to stay. In Florida the homeowner and condominium associations push on all three. HOA Spy indexes 104,659 Florida associations — the 27,377 with a unit count on file hold 1,518,436 homes between them. Their records show 10,296 foreclosure suits the associations brought against their own members, 460,412 claims of lien and 277,047 lis pendens recorded against homes, 48,999 court records in all, and 6,661 associations whose own corporation has lapsed or fallen out of standing. Every count on this page comes from official court dockets and county records, and every community named links to its own record; the dues and price figures are someone else's, dated and linked where they appear. Suits and liens are counts of filings, not of homes lost.

gh-1423101235.s: Debloat any Android or Google TV over Wi-Fi and get an Apple TV-style home.
ex: Strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, and replace the ad-filled home screen with a clean launcher that looks like an Apple TV. No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind. 93 TV models · 31 brands · 17 languages · 370 KB launcher Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: 1. Back up the list of installed packages and settings. 2. Disable the manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk with pm disable-user. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. 3. Install a small native launcher and make it the default home screen. The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use.
